editorial:
Brenda Starr, Reporter is a 13-chapter Columbia Pictures serial from 1945. It adapts Dale Messick's newspaper comic strip. Serial fans and comic-adaptation collectors seek it out as an early screen version of the strip. The Internet Archive item for Part 1 of 13 was confirmed. I did not confirm that the other chapters are hosted there.

The rights trap is that the film does not look like a lapsed copyright. A 1972 Catalog of Copyright Entries volume has renewal-section cross-references for this serial. They cover Chapters 1, 6, 7 and 8. This comes from an OCR text search. The full entries, renewal numbers and dates were not confirmed, and the other chapters were not checked. Each chapter was registered and renewed separately. Treat the chapters as possibly still protected until the entries are confirmed. Copies circulate freely online, but hosting on the Internet Archive does not clear anything. The comic strip underneath is a separate copyright, and I did not check it.
faq: Is Brenda Starr, Reporter (1945) in the public domain?

Unconfirmed. A 1972 Catalog of Copyright Entries volume has renewal-section cross-references for Chapters 1, 6, 7 and 8 of the Columbia serial. The full entries were not verified, and the other chapters were not checked. Each chapter was registered and renewed separately. Treat it as possibly protected. Free copies on the Internet Archive are not a rights clearance.
Can I reuse clips from the Internet Archive copies?

Do not assume you can. Some chapters appear to have renewal entries, and the Dale Messick comic strip is a separate source work. You would need a license from the rights holder, or a legal opinion, before reusing clips commercially.
